- [x] Run-once-at-install seed ops. *(#782 — structural: only the install flow reads `seedOps`)*
- [ ] Converge `adopt-pack` / `adopt-claudinite` onto this runner.

## Phase 4 — Cutover — complete (#785)
- [x] Convert the remaining `agentic:` notes.
  - [x] `pack-independence` — retired as drained (#782), measured against every member's stamp.
  - [x] `prework-rename` — retired (#785). The rollout had dismantled its channel: the canary's first update cycle deleted the record from that member's mount, and the update flows never write the field that held its stamp.
  - [ ] `fleet-baseline-task` (sheepdog) — a **pack** record, so it legitimately keeps its note until the pack flow's apply stage runs it. Verified out of Sheepdog's gap as of 2026-08-12.
- [x] Switch stamp authority from the date to installed versions; retire the held-stamp gating. *(#785 — proven live on Sheepdog: old worker "1 pending note", new worker "agentless night", `updated` released from 2026-08-10 to the real converge time)*

## Phase 5 — Retirement — gated on fleet-wide adoption
- [ ] Remove `packs/basics/tasks/baselining/`, its escalation codes, and its dispatch protocol.
- [ ] Delete the `migrations/apply.mjs` + `migrations/registry.mjs` compatibility entry points (#769).
- [ ] Drop the `agentic:` field from the migration schema.
- [ ] Vocabulary sweep: *baseline/baselining/rebaselining* → *update*.

## The rollout so far
One repo is flipped: **ClaudiniteCanary**, via `maintenance.mechanism: "updates"` ([ClaudiniteCanary#55](https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]Canary/pull/55)). Its first cycle ran the engine flow and the pack flow, opened a PR and merged it in-cycle; baselining, forced on the same repo, stood down. Everything else still declares nothing and is served by baselining, which is the default.

Flipping a further repo needs only that one line — but see the finding below first.

## What the pilot taught, and what it implies for Phase 5
- **A flipped repo leaves the held stamp and the note channel behind.** The update flows never write `claudinite.updated`; they stamp versions. That is why Phase 4 could not wait — on a flipped repo the field would have frozen forever.
- **Read `ref` and the version fields, never `updated`, when judging a member.** A held stamp is indistinguishable from a stale one otherwise; that mistake was made about two healthy members on 2026-08-12 before the hold was retired.
- **A member runs its own vendored worker**, so any mechanism change takes effect one cycle after it lands. Both Sheepdog cycles above demonstrate it, and the skew guard is deliberately built so the lag points at the safe side.

## What the flows share (settled while building)
- A record declares `version` — the owning flow's version its change takes effect at — and lands with that bump. Which flow owns it is structural.
- `migrationApplies` is the single predicate behind fetching, tolerance **and** note selection.
- Unknown installed version → the landed-date window. Unknown is never zero.

- Where a record's decision needs the repo's disk it ships as a **named** codemod, never a general code hatch.
- The self-test gate, the delivery decision and the `needs-human` terminal are shared; the judgment lives with the flow, the token with the shell.
- A default may only point at what is already true (the skew flag's `baselining`).

## Risks

- **The regex-only discipline is a constraint on engine evolution**, accepted explicitly (DESIGN §2.3). Watch for pressure to route around it via "custom updates".

{"number":787,"title":"An update PR that cannot land in-cycle is superseded, not disposed of — the next cycle opens a duplicate","body":"Observed live on TLDR and CrosswordChat while migrating the fleet onto the update mechanism (#768). Both recovered on their own, so this is litter rather than breakage — but it is litter that recurs on every cycle for any member whose PR checks are approval-gated.

## What happens

`engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs` (via the update runner) says what it intends when it cannot land a delivered PR in its own cycle:

```
main requires nothing to merge — skipping the doomed auto-merge arm; waiting for this run's 1 dispatched run(s) and landing PR #246 here
PR #246 not landable this run (no successful run on its head sha) — leaving it open for the next run to dispose of
```

The next run does not dispose of it. It re-runs the flows against a `main` that is still unconverged — precisely because the previous PR never merged — finds work to do, and opens a **new** PR with the same content:

```
merged PR #247 in-cycle — its pull_request run is parked at action_required (never ran) while the dispatched run passed
```

So `main` converges, but the earlier PR is left open forever with a diff that is now already merged. On TLDR that was #246 (superseded by #247); on CrosswordChat, #177 (superseded by #178). Both closed by hand.

## Why the first cycle failed to land

The `pull_request`-triggered check never runs — it is parked at `action_required` by GitHub's approval requirement for bot-authored PRs. The worker correctly detects this and dispatches an equivalent run via `workflow_dispatch` instead, but then gives up on the wait roughly ten seconds before that run reports green. So the failure is a race in the wait, not a broken gate. Widening the wait would fix these two cases and not the general one.

## The actual defect

The promise "leaving it open for the next run to dispose of" has no implementing code path. The runner's early return is:

```js
const changed = git(['-C', root, 'status', '--porcelain']).trim();
if (!changed && terminal.action !== 'needs-human') {
  console.log('update: nothing changed — no branch, no PR');
  return;
}
```

A cycle that finds nothing to do returns *before* looking at open update PRs — so the only cycle that could dispose of a stranded PR is one that has its own work to deliver, and that cycle opens a competing PR instead of landing the old one. Either branch of the condition drops it.

## Suggested shape

Before the converge, have the runner look for an open PR on a `claudinite/update-*` branch and dispose of it first: land it if its head sha now has a successful run, close it if its diff is already in `main`. That makes the sentence in the log true, keeps at most one update PR alive per member, and is the same "dispose of the previous delivery" step baselining effectively gets for free by re-deriving its branch name per day.

Worth deciding at the same time whether the wait should tolerate a check that goes green seconds later, since that is what turned a one-cycle delay into a duplicate here.

## Related

- #768 — the fleet migration that surfaced it.
- #786 — the other finding from the same rollout (`fleet-freshness` measures by a `ref` the update flows never write). Independent bug.
- Member-side note, not a Claudinite bug: TLDR's `test-extension.yml`, `test-requirements.yml` and `test-server.yml` run on `pull_request` with no `workflow_dispatch:` trigger, so delivery cannot start them at all — the worker logged this explicitly for each.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/787","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-12T23:37:43Z","updated_at":"2026-08-12T23:37:43Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":786,"title":"fleet-freshness judges by stamped `ref` age, which the update flows never refresh","body":"Found while migrating the fleet onto `maintenance.mechanism: "updates"` (#768). Not urgent tonight — it starts biting once canon moves past `631a067` and the sweep's age threshold elapses — but it now applies to **every** member rather than one canary.

## The mismatch

`packs/sheepdog/tasks/fleet-freshness/check-fleet-freshness.mjs` takes the age of `claudinite.ref` as the liveness measure, and says so explicitly:

> `claudinite.updated` advances only when canon actually changed that member's vendor set. Age of the STAMPED REF is therefore the honest liveness measure

That was true under baselining, where `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` writes `{updated, ref, engineVersion, packVersions}` on every converge. The update flows write neither `updated` nor `ref`:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` → `next.claudinite = { ...next.claudinite, engineVersion: ENGINE_VERSION }`
- `updates/pack-update.mjs` and `updates/install.mjs` → the same, for `packVersions`

So on a repo served by `updates`, `ref` freezes at whatever baselining last wrote. As canon advances, the freshness sweep will report healthy, fully-current members as increasingly behind, and open `fleet-drift` issues for them — with no signal distinguishing them from a genuinely wedged repo.

## Why "just write `ref` every cycle" is the wrong fix

A no-op update cycle currently produces *no PR at all* — Sheepdog tonight: `update: nothing changed — no branch, no PR`. Stamping a fresh `ref`/`updated` on every converge would put a changed file in every cycle on every member, resurrecting exactly the daily-noise problem the versioned scheme removed. The date-based measure is also strictly weaker than what the member now carries: `engineVersion` and `packVersions` answer "is this current?" exactly, where a date only estimates it.

## Suggested shape

Teach the sweep to branch on the mechanism it already can read from the declaration (`engine/served-by.mjs` is vendored into the enforcer's mount):

- **`baselining`** — unchanged: age of the stamped `ref`.
- **`updates`** — compare `engineVersion` against canon's `ENGINE_VERSION`, and each entry of `packVersions` against that pack's manifest `version`. Behind ⇒ drift, with the gap named. This makes `behind` exact and lets the issue body say *which* version is missing.

The enforcer already fetches canon to resolve the stamped ref against the default branch, so the inputs are in hand.

Open question for the owner, and the reason this is an issue rather than a PR: whether `ref` should still be maintained under `updates` as a debugging fact (which canon commit this mount came from), written only when the converge actually changed files. That keeps no-op cycles silent while preserving provenance — it was `ref` that made tonight's diagnosis possible. It is not needed for the freshness measure above.

## Related

- #768 — the migration; the whole fleet is now on `updates`, which is what makes this fleet-wide.
- missingbulb/Sheepdog#172 — `fleet-baseline` reports `failed: 0` because it counts dispatches, not outcomes. {"number":748,"title":"conformance-backlog: committed-build-artifact check (promote cannot land a check — fixtures sit outside its write surface)","body":"Two things, from the 2026-08-11 `canon-curation/growth-promote` run (#745, PR #747).

## 1. A structural block: promote's ladder cannot reach the check rung

`growth-promote`'s task spec says a lesson a check can carry is **authored as the check** in the promote PR — "the rule module in the right pack, the failure message carrying the generalized lesson, **plus a fixture test proving it fires**".

That is mechanically impossible today:

- promote's write surface is bounded to `packs/` and `skills/`, enforced by `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs` on the `growth-promote` branch prefix;
- a canon pack's fixture test lives under `packs-tests/`, which is **outside** that surface;
- and it cannot move into `packs/` either — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins a closed set of test roots (`engine-tests/`, `packs-tests/`, `vendoring/`, `dev/tools/`, `.claudinite/local/packs/`), with `engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs` failing on any tracked test outside them.

So every promote run must fall back to prose for a convertible rule, and the "prose is the fallback, not the default" ladder never fires. Whichever way it is resolved (widen `inBounds` to `packs-tests/`, or add `packs/` as a test root), it is an owner decision — the run declined to widen its own gate.

## 2. The conversion this blocked

The `.gitignore`-pruning lesson (LaughCounter's local pack, promoted as prose to `git-github-advanced` in #747) converts to a world-scope `basics` check. Written and green locally before being pulled:

- **`packs/basics/committed-build-artifact.mjs`** — advisory, relevance-first. Flags a *tracked* file matching a confined set of artifacts no project tracks on purpose: `__pycache__/`, `*.py[co]`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `*.egg-info/`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`. The `fix` line carries the lesson (delete the artifacts before dropping their ignore rules; read `git diff --cached --stat` after a bulk `git add -A`).
- **`packs-tests/basics/committed-build-artifact.test.mjs`** — four cases: clean tree silent; a swept-in `__pycache__` found; the tool-cache/OS set found; and a narrowness case proving silence on deliberately vendored trees (`node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`) and on prose merely naming `__pycache__`.

Advisory rather than blocking on purpose: the fix is a deletion, and pre-existing junk in a member repo should surface as a finding to clear, not red that repo's sweep and block its maintenance PR.

The set was chosen so the check stays inert on anything a repo might legitimately vendor; `node_modules/` and `dist/` are deliberately excluded.

Refs #745.

{"number":590,"title":"Adoption never sets the two repo settings baselining depends on — add them to bootstrap (both are scriptable)","body":"Baselining's delivery depends on two repository settings that **nothing in adoption ever sets, checks, or mentions**. `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md` has zero references to either — the only mentions anywhere in the corpus are the error strings added by #585.

Both are the direct cause of the two-day fleet stall.

## The settings

| Setting | UI | API |
|---|---|---|
| Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests | Settings → Actions → General | `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions/workflow` → `{"can_approve_pull_request_reviews": true}` |
| Allow auto-merge | Settings → General → Pull Requests | `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}` → `{"allow_auto_merge": true}` |

**Both are readable and writable by script** — plain REST, no UI-only step. The matching `GET` on each returns the current value, so a conformance check could assert them rather than only bootstrap setting them.

The constraint is the credential, not the API: both require **admin** on the repo. The Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot do it, so this cannot be self-healed by baselining from inside the member. It belongs to either:

- **adoption** (`adopt-claudinite`), which already runs in a session with the owner's own credentials, or
- **the sheepdog pack**, whose `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` spans the account — it could converge both settings fleet-wide alongside `fleet-freshness`, and would catch a repo whose settings were later flipped back.

The second is the stronger option: adoption sets it once, whereas the sheepdog sweep keeps it true.

## Why it matters

Without the first, the maintenance PR is never created (#585 — silent before that fix, loud after). Without the second, an `auto-merge` member's PR opens and never lands. Neither is visible from inside the member repo, and neither produced any signal until it was investigated by hand.

## Suggested scope

1. Adoption sets both over the owner's credentials, and records what it set.
2. A check (or the sheepdog freshness sweep) asserts both remain true, reporting the exact API path when they are not.
3. `adopt-claudinite` documents them, so a hand-adopted repo does not silently miss them.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/590","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["quick-win"],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-30T21:42:38Z","updated_at":"2026-08-07T05:30:46Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":649,"title":"A migration cannot materialize a workflow file — baselining's push can never write .github/workflows/","body":"## What happened

The `sheepdog-fleet-baseline` record (landed in #647) materialized `.github/workflows/fleet-baseline.yml` into the enforcer repo. The next baselining run on `missingbulb/Sheepdog` failed at the push:

```
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> claudinite/maintenance-2026-08-05-3fa950
(refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow
 `.github/workflows/fleet-baseline.yml` without `workflows` permission)
```

## The constraint

Baselining's converge pushes with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs:429`). GitHub never lets that token create **or update** anything under `.github/workflows/` — there is no `permissions:` key that grants it. So a migration's `materialize` can never deliver a workflow file, first landing or later edit.

Two consequences, the second worse than the first:

1. **It cannot deliver.** The file has to arrive by a route holding the `workflows` permission — a session using the GitHub MCP tools, which is how missingbulb/Sheepdog#67 landed it.
2. **A rejected push fails the whole converge.** One undeliverable file wedges *everything else* that cycle — mount convergence, wiring, every other migration note — and it re-wedges on every subsequent run. The member goes quiet except for `needs-human` issues.

`chrome-release-vendoring` and `static-site-vendoring` both carry workflow materializations and have not hit this only because their copies are already in place and byte-identical, so `applyMaterializations` writes nothing. **Either record wedges its repos the day its template changes.** That is the live hazard here, not the sheepdog record specifically — that one is being removed.

## Options

- **Agentic note.** Drop `materialize` for workflow paths and carry an `agentic: { model, instructions }` note instead. Baselining's agent stage already writes through `mcp__github__*`, which holds the `workflows` permission — so the existing primitive covers exactly this gap. Probably the durable answer.
- **Make the converge survive it.** Detect a write under `.github/workflows/` before pushing, drop it from the commit, land everything else, and surface one issue naming the files a human must land. Fixes the wedge regardless of how delivery is solved.
- **Guard at authoring time.** A conformance check can't do this cleanly today: `runRule` is synchronous (`engine/checks/helpers/work.mjs:21`) while `loadMigrations`/`appliesTo` are async, so a check cannot tell a *pending* materialization from a settled one. It would need async check support, or a coarser "no migration materializes into `.github/workflows/`" rule that the two existing records would violate.

The second option is worth doing on its own merits even if the first lands: a converge that can be wedged by one unpushable path is fragile in a way that is not specific to workflows.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/649","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"comments":5,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-05T17:23:41Z","updated_at":"2026-08-07T03:50:22Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":625,"title":"static-website: a repo's own values should reach build_command as environment variables","body":"All three of our site repos hand-roll the same step in their own deploy workflow: substitute a Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon token, held in the repo variable `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`, into the served `analytics.js`. {"number":379,"title":"Vendored-mount flip isn't fleet-ready: MCP push_files can't land the canon vendor in one commit, fixed-branch re-dispatch races, and the .claude write prompt suspends unattended runs (GCEC pilot)","body":"The 2026-07-21 fleet daily maintenance run attempted the `vendored-mount-flip` on its sole pilot member (`flip.repos: ['missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator']`). It failed on **structural** grounds, not a one-off fluke. GCEC's `main` was never touched (still pre-flip, legacy `.claudinite/mount`, no stamp) so nothing is broken — but the flip mechanism is not ready to run unattended or to widen.

## What happened
The flip must vendor the entire canon snapshot — `.claudinite/shared/**`, ~240 KB across hundreds of files — into the member. The migration/worker contract says land **one** content commit (then a separate `delete_file` for the legacy hook). In practice:

1. **`push_files` can't carry the vendor tree in one commit (size limit).** The worker fell back to committing in batches — `Claudinite: vendor the canon snapshot (batch 1/11)`, `2/11`, `3/11`, … — directly contradicting the "one content commit" contract. Any batching here must be deterministic, idempotent, and resumable; today it isn't specified.

2. **The fixed `claudinite/maintenance` branch races under re-dispatch.** The first attempt suspended on the `.claude/settings.json` permission prompt (see #3); a second worker was dispatched while the first was still live, and **both wrote the same fixed branch with different batch plans** — the log interleaves `batch 3/11`, then `batch 2/10`, then `batch 4/11` (two denominators = two writers). A fixed, shared branch name has no single-writer guarantee; re-dispatch duplicates/races. Needs a per-attempt branch or a real single-writer/idempotent-convergence guard.

3. **The `.claude/settings.json` write suspends an unattended run indefinitely.** Repointing the SessionStart/Stop/PreToolUse hooks triggers an interactive permission prompt. Unanswered, it left the worker idle for ~hours (surfaced as a bogus multi-hour "runtime"). The flip cannot be an unattended nightly operation while that prompt exists — it must be gated to an attended path or a pre-authorized allow-rule.

4. **A batched/raced landing leaves an ambiguous half-flipped branch.** The abandoned branch had `.claudinite/shared/` only partially vendored, the legacy `.claudinite/mount` **not** deleted, no `claudinite` stamp, and no PR. The preconditions (pre-flip / half-flipped / flipped) assume a near-atomic landing and don't cover "partial vendor from a batched/raced push."

5. **Cleanup gap: the fleet session can't delete the junk branch.** After a failed flip, the abandoned `claudinite/maintenance` branch can't be removed from the maintenance session — the git proxy `403`s a branch-delete push and the GitHub MCP exposes no delete-branch / delete-ref tool (only `create_branch`). So even cleanup after a failed flip needs a manual step.

## Recommendation
- **Do not widen `flip.repos`** beyond the pilot, and treat the flip as **not nightly-ready**.
- Before retrying: (a) an MCP-batch-aware *or* alternative landing that survives `push_files` limits, deterministic + resumable; (b) single-writer / per-attempt-branch handling so re-dispatch can't race; (c) move the `.claude/settings.json` write behind an attended or pre-authorized gate; (d) precondition handling for a partially-vendored branch; (e) a way for the session to delete an abandoned flip branch (or avoid creating one until the landing is atomic).

## Housekeeping
- GCEC `main` is safe (pre-flip, coherent). No cleanup needed there.
- The abandoned `missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator` branch `claudinite/maintenance` (5 orphan "vendor the canon snapshot" commits, no PR) needs **manual deletion** — the session couldn't remove it (see #5).

Relates to #315 (vendored-mount design), #335 (flip strands docs / phase-3 sweep). Source: the `2026-07-18-vendored-mount-flip` note.

{"number":409,"title":"Tracking-issue freshness: keep the plan issue in sync after every merge","body":"Implementation tracker for the tracking-issue freshness check. This issue is itself an instance of the pattern it tracks — it carries the live checklist; the committed doc carries the rationale.

**Read first (on `main`):**
- Design + plan — [`docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/blob/main/docs/tracking-issue-freshness/DESIGN.md)

**The problem:** a major task has two artifacts — a source-controlled design/migration plan and a GitHub tracking issue with a `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checklist (the "read status and pick up the work" point). When a phase lands, the committed plan's status is updated in the same PR (the diff forces review), but the issue checklist is a separate surface no diff touches, so it silently drifts. Already live: `per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md` says Phase 1 is "same day, no soak" while #394's Phase 1 item still says "Soak ~1 week."

**The design, in two surfaces:**
1. **In-session (timely):** a transcript-only post-merge check-the-work rule — `in-session-github-access` (blocking) means in-session code has no GitHub REST credential, so the rule reads the merge, the tracker discovery, and the post-merge checklist edit from the session transcript's MCP tool calls. Enablers: `work.mergedThisSession()` and a Stop-hook post-merge trigger (the merge recipe leaves a clean tree, which would otherwise fast-exit).
2. **Nightly (convergent):** plans state, per phase, *how completion is decided* — a checklist item may carry `` naming a dependency-free Node script whose **exit 0 means the phase is done** ("if this code passes, phase 3 is done"); no marker ⇒ the phase's prose **Verify** block in the plan doc is the criteria. The `plan-status-update` task (daily, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue) re-derives every tracker's checklist from these verifiers — flipping what sessions missed, flagging (never auto-un-flipping) a checked item whose code verifier now fails.

**Invariant:** any open `plan-tracking` issue must carry a todo checklist and have a box **flipped** in the same session as each merge that advances it (after the merge, not before — an item isn't done until it's on `main`). The issue *count* is not enforced.

**Phases (detail in the design doc):**
- [ ] **Convention + seed** — define the `plan-tracking` label and its meaning in the `grow_with_claudinite` / merge docs; apply it to existing in-flight tracker(s) (#394).
- [ ] **Primitive + trigger** — `work.mergedThisSession()` (transcript-derived accepted PRs) and the Stop hook's post-merge trigger, each with red-first tests.
- [ ] **Verifier (in-session)** — the `plan-tracking-freshness` rule in `grow_with_claudinite`; fires when a merge happened with no post-merge checklist flip, quiet otherwise.
- [ ] **Recipe wiring** — `merge-to-main` gains the "sync the `plan-tracking` issue after the merge" step (prose asks; the check guarantees).
- [ ] **Docs** — the convention in the pack README; design-doc status box; this issue points at the doc.
- [ ] **Per-phase verifiers (convention)** — `` code verifiers (exit 0 ⇒ done) with prose Verify blocks as fallback; recorded in the pack README and the nightly worker doc.
- [ ] **Nightly status update** — the `plan-status-update` task (daily/sonnet/none, gated on an open `plan-tracking` issue): re-verifies each tracker, flips passes, flags regressions in a comment.

**Decisions (resolved with the owner):** label = `plan-tracking`; issue count not enforced; a **checkbox flip** is required (a bare comment isn't enough); label precision from the transcript for the in-session rule; the once-contingent world-scope backstop is **superseded** by the nightly task, which runs with the executor session's MCP credential and has no label blind spot.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/409","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["plan-tracking"],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-23T09:56:23Z","updated_at":"2026-07-30T04:45:55Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false,"closed_by_pull_requests":{"total_count":0,"references":[]}}

{"number":564,"title":"Pack manifests as JSON: pack.json + pack.schema.json, code split into sibling files","body":"Owner comment (process-change): "Why are packs declared using mjs? Is it just the `detect` part? It seems they can all be just JSON declarations, and if we have some code that detects, we can put that in a different file. And once it's just JSON — can't you declare the schema in a nicer way than `engine/pack_loader/pack-schema.mjs`? You can still have validations (a simple unit test) for making sure all the skills/rules are declared and there's no drift, but at least the files will be sane."

Measured across the 29 manifests (27 canon + the home's 2 local packs): **988 lines, 56 of them `import` statements, 350 of them comments.** Almost nothing in a `pack.mjs` needs to be code.

## What is actually code today

| Field | Packs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `detect` | 13 (14 declare `null`) | ~10 are one-liners over `ctx.tracked` — `includes`, `endsWith`, a path regex, or the shared `hasMarkerNearRoot` helper — all expressible as data. **3 need real logic**: `chrome-extension` (locates the extension manifest), `chrome-extension-release` (recognizes a release orchestrator workflow), `leaflet` (scans file *content*). |
| `worldRules` / `workRules` | all | Code only as *imports*. In JSON these become filenames the loader imports. |
| `env` | 2 | Genuinely code — `setup`/`probe` are functions of the pack's config returning shell. |
| `contributes` / `contributedRules` | 3 / 1 | `contributes` is a map of pack id → rule modules, so filenames. `contributedRules` (barriers only) is a real seam. |
| everything else | — | Pure data: `id`, `badge`, `marker`, `prose`, `seededByDefault`, `requires`, `ruleRoutingGuidance`, `skills`, `questions`. |

## Shape wanted

- `packs//pack.json` for all 29, with `$schema` pointing at a `pack.schema.json`.
- Optional sibling code files, named from the JSON, only where needed: `detect.mjs` (3 packs), `env.mjs` (2), `contributed-rules.mjs` (1).
- Rules referenced **by filename**, which buys a drift guard the current shape cannot have: every rule `.mjs` in the pack directory must appear in exactly one of the two scope lists. Today an undeclared rule module is simply invisible.

## Why it is worth more than tidiness

**The loader stops executing arbitrary code at load.** Today a consumer's local `pack.mjs` is `import()`ed during SessionStart in every session and on every check run — which is precisely why `pack-registry.mjs` carries per-pack import isolation. With JSON, the ~26 packs that need no code execute none.

**A real schema.** `pack.schema.json` gives editor autocomplete and validation that `PACK_FIELDS` never will.

## What it costs

1. **The 350 comment lines have nowhere to go** — and they are real rationale, not noise: why `basics` requires `barriers` and contributes the isolation barrier as manifest data, why `canon-curation`'s declaration cardinality is what makes its tasks central-once. The natural home is the pack README, which is now exactly the "rationale the manifest cannot carry" file after #559 — this brings two or three of the deleted ones back.
2. **`pack.mjs` is a consumer-held shape**, not only ours — every member repo has local packs. Needs both-shapes tolerance plus a baseline migration to retire the old one, per `consumer-safe-changes.md`.

## Scope note on validation

A consumer's local pack must be validated at *their* Stop hook, not this repo's CI, so loader-side validation stays. JSON Schema replaces the **field-shape** half of `pack-schema.mjs`; the **cross-file drift guards** (skills ↔ directory, rules ↔ files) remain loader checks with unit tests over them. Net effect: that module shrinks substantially rather than disappearing.

{"number":498,"title":"scheduler-workflow-shape should validate the scopes a repo's tasks actually need, not a fixed two","body":"Surfaced by the `growth-extract` run on #484, and pulled out of that run's RULES.md entries during review: this reads as a proposed mechanism change rather than a rule a session can follow, so filing it here instead.

## The gap

`packs/basics/scheduler-workflow-shape.mjs` validates exactly two permissions on a repo's `claudinite-scheduler.yml`, both hard-coded:

```
if (!/^\s*contents:\s*write\b/m.test(text))       → flag
if (!/^\s*pull-requests:\s*write\b/m.test(text))  → flag
```

Those two cover baselining's `deliver()` (push a branch, open a PR, arm auto-merge). They cover nothing a *task's worker* needs. So a task whose worker calls a GitHub endpoint requiring some third scope passes the check with a stub that never granted it, and the failure lands at runtime in a member repo.

## How it actually bit (#478)

`store-release`'s worker POSTs a `workflow_dispatch`, which needs `actions: write`. The stub granted `actions: read`. Every fire 403'd, the worker exited 1, and the scheduler converged the task to `needs-human` — leaving three cut-over members with no working release path. Nothing caught it earlier because nothing was looking: the check validates a fixed pair, and the next task needing a fourth scope will land exactly the same way.

## Suggested direction

Make the required scope set *derived* rather than fixed. Roughly:

1. Let a task declare what its worker needs in its `task.mjs` — e.g. `required_scopes: ['actions:write']` — alongside the existing `agent_model` / `expected_outcome` fields, validated by `task-contract.mjs`.
2. Have `scheduler-workflow-shape` union the declared scopes across the repo's enabled tasks with the baselining floor (`contents:write`, `pull-requests:write`) and assert the workflow grants each one, naming the task that needs it in the failure message.
3. Have the stub generator emit the union, so a repo that adopts a task gets the grant with it rather than hand-editing `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml`.

That turns "read the scope off the endpoint and grant it yourself, and hope you remembered" into a declaration the check enforces. Worth weighing against the simpler option — keep the check fixed but widen the floor to include `actions: write` — which costs a broader default token but no new contract surface.

Not started; opening for a decision on which direction (or neither) before any implementation.

{"number":422,"title":"Wire the canon's executor Routines (self + fleet) — last step of the scheduler cutover","body":"The canon's own scheduler landed in #421 (Refs #394). The scheduler evaluates the canon's tasks hourly; agentless ones run inline (`baselining` self-skips, `migrations-retire` archives), and agentful ones file `[claudinite-task]` issues for an **executor Routine** to run. Executor Routines are a Claude Code Routine + settings change, not code — the one remaining manual step.

Per the **self/fleet split** (#421), there are **two** executors, distinguished by trigger label, so the fleet-wide session grant stays off the self executor:

### 1. Self executor — every repo (incl. the canon)
```
Name:            Claudinite executor
Trigger:         GitHub issue-label event — `ready-for-agent` applied
Session model:   sonnet
Launcher prompt: Execute the Claudinite executor: engine/scheduler/executor.md
Sources:         [REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]  (this repo alone — self tasks touch only their own repo)
```
Runs: `growth-extract`, `growth-dedup`, `conversation-extract`, `growth-discover-packs`, `prose-to-checks-sweep`, `repo-tidy`. **A Routine (poke-only base) was created — `Claudinite executor` (`trig_01S7nEHSd4eQ2832jLDjdSEz`).** Finish it in settings: attach the **GitHub connector** (required — the created Routine stored none, so it'd run without `mcp__github__*`), set the trigger to the `ready-for-agent` label, model `sonnet`, sources = Claudinite alone.

### 2. Fleet executor — only repos with a fleet task (today: the canon)
```
Name:            Claudinite executor (fleet)
Trigger:         GitHub issue-label event — `ready-for-agent-fleet` applied
Session model:   sonnet
Launcher prompt: Execute the Claudinite executor: engine/scheduler/executor.md
Sources:         the owner's repos  (a fleet task reads across them — e.g. growth-promote reads every member's local packs)
```
Runs: `growth-promote` only. Same settings to finish (GitHub connector, label filter `ready-for-agent-fleet`, model `sonnet`, broader sources).

### Notes
- **Canon path:** both prompts use `engine/scheduler/executor.md` (repo root) — the canon runs its own engine, no vendored mount. (A consumer's self executor would use `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/executor.md`; `executor.md` resolves this itself.)
- **Labels:** the scheduler creates `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-agent-fleet`, `agent-running`, `needs-human`, `workflow-failure` on its first dispatch (create-if-missing). ## Decision (agreed with owner)

- **Hosting model: vendor into each consumer.** GitHub only resolves reusable workflows/composite actions from a repo's own `.github/`, never from a `packs/…` subdir, so "into the pack" means the pack holds the templates and each consumer hosts a *managed* copy in its own `.github/`. Consumers become self-contained; baselining (not the consumer) owns keeping the copies correct. This reverses the original "thin consumer" design — deliberately.
- **Phase-2 deletion: automatic, telemetry-gated.** Once the fleet census confirms every consumer has vendored, the census deletes Claudinite's release plumbing automatically as part of migration retirement — no follow-up PR.
- **Secrets: nothing to migrate.** The four `CHROME_*` secrets already live in each consumer repo (they travel via `secrets: inherit` from the consumer's own workflow); Claudinite holds none.

## Plan

1. **Pack = source of truth.** Move the 4 workflows + 3 composite actions into `packs/chrome-extension-release/` as vendored templates; rewrite cross-repo `uses: [REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/.github/…@main` → local `uses: ./.github/…`; rename to avoid the in-repo filename collision (the orchestrator and the create-package reusable are both `chrome-extension-release.yml` today).

Extend the migration mechanism (today rename-only) with the materialize op, and teach the census to delete the home-repo files on retirement.
3. **Tolerant checks during transition.** The `cer/*` checks accept both the old thin-stub shape and the new vendored shape until the migration retires, so no consumer's check suite goes red mid-flight.
4. **Docs.** Update `RELEASE.md`, `.github/workflows/README.md` (drop the frozen-`@main`-API section), and the pack fingerprint.

## Prerequisite for the automatic cut

The automatic phase-2 deletion needs `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` granted **Contents-write on the home repo** — #239 notes this is not granted yet. Until it is, the census logs "grant FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN Contents write" and Claudinite's copies stay in place (harmless — consumers already run off their vendored copies by then).

### 2. RELEASE — chrome-extension-release infra hosted in core `.github/`
The reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml`) and the `read-release-config` action live in the core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. **Decide:** whether this plumbing should move to live behind the pack that owns it, or is legitimately shared canon CI.

`checks/DESIGN.md`, `extending.md`, `growth/*.md`, `README.md`, `consumer-safe-changes.md`, etc. cite specific packs/skills by name as illustrative examples (e.g. "per the `unattended-agents` skill", "e.g. the `tidy-repo` pack"). If the Action model is preferred, that's a contained follow-up (a workflow + token, independent of the sheepdog census).

{"number":170,"title":"Revisit: Workflow tool's interactive opt-in blocks unattended routines (waiting on Anthropic)","body":"## The limitation

The multi-agent-orchestration **`Workflow`** tool requires an **interactive human opt-in on every run** ("Allow Claude to run a workflow?"). That prompt only disappears under bypass-permissions / headless modes a scheduler can't be relied on to be in. Because an unattended routine has no human to click **Allow**, any routine that fans out through the Workflow tool stalls on step one.

This also means the tool's nicest ergonomics are off-limits to us for unattended work: committing a Workflow script and having the nightly job just run it by name (`Workflow({name: ...})`) hits the **same** prompt — the gate is on *invoking* a workflow, not on authoring one. And the parallel-agent step can't be pushed into a plain committed script either, since spawning Claude subagents is a harness capability, not something arbitrary code can call.

## Our current workaround

We fan the fleet daily maintenance routine out with **plain subagent dispatch** (the Agent/Task tool) instead, which carries no opt-in gate, and the orchestrator honors the phase barriers itself. See #168 / #169 and `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md` + `skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md`.

This works and is the right default (no dependency on an out-of-repo permission-mode setting), but it costs us the Workflow tool's built-in phase/barrier machinery and the option to run committed, reviewed orchestration code.

## Why keep this open

This is a limitation of the platform, not our code — we're **waiting on the world to change**. If Anthropic later lets an unattended session pre-authorize the Workflow tool (a settings allowlist entry, an environment/routine permission mode that reliably suppresses just this prompt, or persisted per-workflow consent that survives a fresh cloud clone), we could reconsider using committed Workflow scripts for the fleet routine and get determinism + review back.

**Action:** periodically check with Anthropic / the Claude Code release notes whether the Workflow tool can be pre-authorized for unattended sessions. When it can, revisit the plain-dispatch decision in the routine spec.

Portable, project-agnostic practices for building Chrome (and Chromium) extensions — manifest
versions, background/service workers, content scripts, permissions, packaging and store review —
true for any extension read cold.

> **Releasing, versioning, and Chrome Web Store publication are standardized** — before building
> or changing any release/publish machinery in an extension repo, read the
> [chrome-extension-release standard](../chrome-extension-release/RELEASE.md) (its pack, declared
> when you're ready to ship) and copy its canonical workflows instead of re-deriving them.

## Service worker

- **Handing a path to a Chrome API or `fetch` from an MV3 service worker** (`importScripts`,
  `action.setIcon`) — make it extension-root absolute: a leading slash, or
  `chrome.runtime.getURL(...)`. A worker's relative paths resolve against the worker's **own** file
  location, not the extension root, and a bare relative path fails silently — it can abort the
  worker on import, or make an API call reject while the worker keeps running.

- **Wanting `import`/`export` in extension code** — MV3 loads ES modules natively; don't add a
  bundler just to use them. Declare the service worker `"type": "module"` and load page/side-panel
  scripts with `<script type="module">`; relative imports resolve within the packaged extension.
  Content scripts are the exception — they are classic scripts, below.

## Content scripts

- **Assembling a shared global from several injected content-script files** — **augment** it,
  never replace it: merge onto it (e.g. `Object.assign`), not `globalThis.X = {...}`. The files are
  re-injected into the page on every activation (e.g. every popup open), so replacing makes each
  newly-injected file wipe what earlier files already attached.

- **Accumulating state in a file that is re-injected** (e.g. a list a source pushes into) — reset
  it at load time.

- **Loading ES module code into a content script** — register a tiny **classic loader** whose only
  statement is a *dynamic* `import(chrome.runtime.getURL('…'))`. A **registered or static content
  script runs as a *classic* script — it can't be an ES module**:
  `chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts` and static `content_scripts` inject their files as
  classic scripts (there is no `type: 'module'` mode, unlike a page's `<script type="module">` or
  the module service worker), so a top-level `import` in one throws
  `Uncaught SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` — **in the host page's
  console, not the extension's**. Dynamic `import()` is legal in a classic script, and the module it
  pulls in runs in the same content-script isolated world with the content-script `chrome.*` surface
  intact.

- **Adding an import to a content-script module** — list that module **and its whole transitive
  import graph** under `web_accessible_resources` (gated to the target origins), or the fetch is
  blocked.

- **Keeping that `web_accessible_resources` list correct** — have a test walk the import graph
  from the entry module, so a newly-added import can't silently fall out of the list.

## Permissions and host access

- **Matching a host with `chrome.events.UrlFilter`** — its host operators are **raw string
  matches, not domain-boundary matches**: `hostSuffix: "example.com"` also matches
  `evilexample.com`, and `declarativeContent`'s `PageStateMatcher.pageUrl` gates an action icon or
  page condition on exactly these filters. To mean *apex-or-any-subdomain*, combine
  `hostEquals: "example.com"` with `hostSuffix: ".example.com"` (the leading dot forces a label
  boundary); never gate a security- or origin-sensitive behavior on a bare `hostSuffix`.

- **Running a content script on arbitrary third-party pages without an install-time host warning**
  — request access at runtime: declare the origins under `optional_host_permissions` plus the
  (silent) `scripting` permission, call `chrome.permissions.request()` **synchronously inside a real
  foreground user gesture** (Chrome rejects the request from a service-worker message handler), then
  register the script dynamically with `chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts()` — never a
  static `content_scripts` entry.

- **Starting the service worker when a runtime-granted permission is in play** — reconcile your
  stored enabled-flag against the permission actually granted and re-register (or clean up) to
  match, on every start. The grant can be revoked from `chrome://extensions` out from under you.

- **A fetch to a host you listed failing in-browser** — `host_permissions` does not bypass CORS.
  Listing a host lets the extension's fetches *reach* it, but the server must still return CORS
  headers for the extension origin (`chrome-extension://<id>`) or the request fails.

- **Reaching your *own* backend** — don't add a `host_permissions` entry merely for that: if it
  already returns permissive CORS the fetch succeeds without one, and the entry only adds a scary
  install-time host-access warning.

## Sign-in and tokens

- **Authenticating an extension to a JWT-validating backend** (an API Gateway JWT authorizer, any
  OIDC-validating server) — obtain a Google **ID token** with `chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow`
  (`response_type=id_token`) against a Google Cloud OAuth client of type **Web application**,
  redirect to `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/` (from `chrome.identity.getRedirectURL()`),
  scope `openid email profile`, and **verify the returned `nonce`**. Pin the extension id with a
  manifest `key` so the redirect URI stays fixed. Do **not** use `chrome.identity.getAuthToken` —
  it returns an opaque OAuth *access* token (no verifiable signature/`iss`/`aud`) that a JWT
  authorizer rejects.

- **Refreshing a token silently** (`launchWebAuthFlow({interactive:false})`) — request
  `prompt=none`. `prompt=consent` always needs interaction and therefore always fails silently —
  reserve it (or omit `prompt`) for the interactive fallback.

- **Refreshing silently with more than one account signed in** — pass the remembered account's
  email as `login_hint`; otherwise the provider can't tell which session to reuse and forces an
  interactive account-picker. Persist the non-secret email from the first successful sign-in.

- **Storing a token** — extension storage is unencrypted, so treat tokens as secrets at rest: keep
  the bearer/ID token in in-memory `chrome.storage.session` (cleared on browser exit) and persist
  only non-secret identifiers (e.g. the account email) to `chrome.storage.local`.

- **Wanting a token to survive a browser restart** — re-run the silent flow; don't switch to a
  refresh-token flow just for that, which puts a longer-lived credential on disk.

## Extension UI surfaces

- **Knowing whether your side panel is open** — have the panel open a `Port` on load and read its
  connect/disconnect as open/closed. MV3 gives the side panel no is-open/close API, and an action
  popup suppresses `action.onClicked`.

- **Opening the side panel programmatically** — `chrome.sidePanel.open()` needs Chrome 116+, so
  raise `minimum_chrome_version` accordingly.

- **Putting a menu on the toolbar icon itself** — create it with
  `chrome.contextMenus.create({ contexts: ['action'], … })`; the `contextMenus` permission carries
  **no** install-time warning (unlike a broad host permission).

- **Recreating those menu items on install or startup** — call `contextMenus.removeAll()` first,
  so they self-heal instead of throwing on duplicate ids when the service worker re-runs its top
  level.

## Introspecting a service worker over CDP

- **Awaiting a `chrome.*` callback API inside `Runtime.evaluate`** — don't: they don't reliably
  settle when awaited with `awaitPromise: true` (a hang with no internal timeout). Build the awaited
  signal from plain promises (`fetch`/`OffscreenCanvas`) instead.

- **Reading a worker value from an injected evaluate** — a bare top-level `function`/`const` isn't
  reachable from one, so expose what the probe reads as an explicit `globalThis.x = …`.

- **Attaching to a dormant worker** — poll for the global rather than reading it once immediately
  after attaching. A dormant worker has no globals until it re-runs its top level, and attaching to
